item.title: Tyler Bates is Jumping Ship from Marilyn Manson’s Touring Lineup to Focus on the Big Screen
item.description: It looks like the Marilyn Manson live experience is going to look a little different moving forward. Tyler Bates, the multi-instrumentalist mastermind who has been a cornerstone of Manson’s sound for the better part of a decade, has officially decided to hang up his touring boots.

item.title: Killswitch Engage's JESSE LEACH Reflects On Tour Life: 'We Owe It To The Fans, Dude'
item.description: Killswitch Engage singer Jesse Leach opened up about the pressures of touring and how he protects his voice on the road. In a recent interview with American Musical Supply, Leach explained his routine for staying healthy and keeping his vocals in shape while traveling.

item.title: SOAD's SHAVO ODADJIAN Says Phone Bans At Shows 'Take Something Away' From Fans: 'I Catch Myself Filming Sometimes Too'
item.description: Shavo Odadjian, bassist of System of a Down, doesn’t believe in taking away your phone at a concert. In a recent Q&A with readers of Metal Hammer, Odadjian shared his thoughts on phone-free shows, a practice growing in popularity among artists looking to keep fans more engaged during live performances.

item.title: Evanescence's AMY LEE Reflects On Pandemic-Era Lessons: 'Who Knows When This Will Ever End? So Let’s Put Out Our Music'
item.description: Amy Lee says the pandemic changed how Evanescence approaches releasing music. In a recent interview with WDHA-FM, the singer explained that waiting for a perfect moment to drop a full album no longer feels realistic.

item.title: AMY LEE Says New EVANESCENCE Album Coming 'Probably Early Next Year'
item.description: Evanescence is working on their next studio album, and according to Amy Lee, it’s likely to arrive in early 2026. The singer gave an update during a recent interview with WDHA-FM 105.

item.title: THE BAND That Toured With Guns N’ Roses and Wished They Hadn’t: 'I Don’t Want To Be Around Them'
item.description: In the early ’90s, opening for Guns N’ Roses was considered a golden ticket, massive crowds, media buzz, and a shot at mainstream fame. For Soundgarden, a loud and rising band from Seattle, the offer felt like a fast pass out of the grunge underground.
